items.headline: Oklo's first Aurora startup window widens to 2028 to 2029
items.what_happened: On its Q3 2026 results and call, Oklo said its first Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory may not begin operating until 2028 or 2029, against a firm 2028 target it had repeated before. CEO Jake DeWitte tied the added time to commissioning and calibration lessons from the Groves-1 test reactor. He expects the documented safety analysis to move forward closer to construction completion, likely in 2028.
items.why_it_matters: A buyer counting on Aurora for 2028 power should treat 2029 as a live case. The schedule now comes with a range, not a date, and the design's first-of-a-kind timeline is the main open risk.
items.binding_note: A schedule statement made on the earnings call and in the quarterly filing. It is not a contract, order or completed milestone.
